what_it_does: When chip designers want to find the best CPU configuration — the right number of cores, cache sizes, pipeline depth, and so on — they face a huge search space called design space exploration (DSE). A common shortcut is to train a machine-learning model on one program's behavior and use it to predict performance for other programs, but the model often overfits (learns too narrowly) or fails because different programs stress the chip in very different ways. MetaDSE treats this as a 'few-shot' problem: instead of retraining from scratch for each new program, it uses a technique called MAML (Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning) that trains a model to learn quickly from just a handful of examples of any new program. It also introduces a filtering step called an 'architectural mask' that highlights which design knobs actually matter for a given program, ignoring irrelevant ones so the model isn't confused by noise.
